classification.difficultyReason: Combines the sine rule and triangle area formula to establish a symbolic result.

content.prompt:
For triangle $ABC$, show that
$$\text{Area}=\frac{a^2\sin B\sin C}{2\sin A}.$$

spec.description: Unfilled labelled triangle ABC; ordinary source blue outlines rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AB=c, BC=a, AC=b; no numerical givens or angle marks.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle \text{Area}=\frac12 ac\sin B=\frac{a^2\sin B\sin C}{2\sin A}$.

Substitute $c=\frac{a\sin C}{\sin A}$ from the sine rule.
answer.worked:
By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}c&=\frac{a\sin C}{\sin A}.\end{align*}$$
Using the area rule,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12 ac\sin B\\\text{Area}&=\frac12 a\left(\frac{a\sin C}{\sin A}\right)\sin B\\\text{Area}&=\frac{a^2\sin B\sin C}{2\sin A}.\end{align*}$$
